subject: Azure Marketplace private offer: SKU packaging, rebate phasing & channel commission waterfall
messages:
From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
To: shelly.park@acmetech.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure Marketplace private offer: SKU packaging, rebate phasing & channel commission waterfall

Hi Shelly —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our call, I wanted to put the proposal in writing so procurement has a single view of the ask and our suggested structure. High-level:

- Offer scope: Azure private offer for Core and Premium SKUs (Core = base tokens, Premium = dedicated throughput and priority burst).
- Pricing ask: 18% off list for Core, 28% off list for Premium for year 1.
- Channel margin: Acme resellers will receive a two-tranche commission (10% pass-through at invoice + 3% retro rebate at true-up if usage exceeds threshold).
- Rebate phasing: We propose a 60/40 phased rebate to smooth initial recognition (60% at quarter 1 true-up, 40% at year-end true-up).

Attached is a worked example (pricing-model-v2.xlsx) with monthly consumption scenarios and revenue waterfall to show net-back to Acme and partner. A couple of asks for procurement:

1) Confirm whether the reseller needs the commission to flow via the Marketplace invoice or via a separate reseller agreement (this affects our invoicing cadence).
2) Confirm any PO terms around billing frequency (monthly vs quarterly).
3) Any legal/regulatory clauses Acme requires for data residency in the Azure Gov/Enterprise regions — we included placeholders in the draft PO.

Ben and Laura are copied on this note — Ben can surface the channel math and Laura will scope support for Marketplace listing and SKU mapping.

If that reads right, can you confirm by EOD Wednesday and I’ll circulate a clean PO draft?

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0186

From: Shelly Park <shelly.park@acmetech.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmetech.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace private offer: SKU packaging, rebate phasing & channel commission waterfall

Thanks Stephanie — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from procurement:

1) You called out a 10% invoice-level pass-through + 3% retro. Can you show the net price if the reseller requires 13% upfront (i.e., they cannot wait for a true-up)? Our finance team needs the cash-flow view.
2) For the 60/40 phasing, is the Q1 true-up tied to an absolute usage threshold or a growth relative to baseline? We prefer absolute thresholds to avoid disputes.
3) We need to confirm whether Premium SKU licensing can be consumed across multiple subscriptions under our master tenant — does Redwood support org-wide SSO billing?

CCing procurement mailbox to track. If we can get a simple table that shows list price, customer net after reseller, reseller gross, and Redwood net (post-commissions & rebates) at Low/Med/High consumption, we can move to the PO quickly.

Shelly
Shelly Park
Senior Procurement Manager
AcmeTech

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: shelly.park@acmetech.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace private offer: SKU packaging, rebate phasing & channel commission waterfall

Shelly —

Thanks for the quick follow. I attached a revised tab in pricing-model-v2.xlsx that shows both scenarios: (A) 10% invoice pass-through + 3% true-up and (B) 13% upfront on invoice. Quick callouts:

- Scenario A improves Redwood cash flow slightly (because the 3% true-up is deferred) but lowers reseller realized margin at the time of invoice. Scenario B gives resellers immediate cash but reduces Redwood margin in year 1.
- For modeling I used an absolute threshold of 2M tokens/month for the Q1 true-up trigger. We can dial that up/down — we recommended 2M to be conservative given your projected run-rate.
- Premium SKU can be licensed across multiple subscriptions under a single tenant; billing is per-tenant but usage aggregation is supported for Marketplace private offers. We’ll note this in the PO.

Next steps I suggest: Stephanie to share the clean PO (acme-po-draft.docx) and we iterate on the revenue waterfall line items. If Acme prefers the reseller commission to be paid outside Marketplace, we’ll need the partner agreement and we'll convert the flow accordingly.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Manager, GTM Finance
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

(attachment: pricing-model-v2.xlsx)

From: Shelly Park <shelly.park@acmetech.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmetech.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace private offer: SKU packaging, rebate phasing & channel commission waterfall

Appreciate the detail — the dual-scenario tab is exactly what we needed. Procurement is comfortable moving forward with Scenario B (13% on-invoice to reseller) provided Redwood can protect a minimum list-price floor for the Premium SKU in Q1. Two outstanding asks before we sign:

1) Please confirm the minimum list-price floor language in the draft PO (we’ll mark it as Section 3.2).
2) Confirm that the 3% retro rebate (if any) will be applied as a credit on the next billing cycle if usage requirements are met (we prefer credits vs. one-off refunds).

If you can update acme-po-draft.docx with Section 3.2 and the credit language I’ll route to legal and we should have signature within 10 business days.

Shelly
